Reference.title: MITRE ATT and CK - T1595 Active Scanning

ExecutiveSummary.Overview: NETSCOUT Arbor Edge Defense flagged an external source IP as a scanner ("*scan*" / threat category "Network Scanners") probing JCB internet-facing services. Triage question: is this targeted reconnaissance staging an attack against the bank (an APT mapping attack surface), or ubiquitous internet background scanning that AED already blocked?
ExecutiveSummary.BusinessImpact: Reconnaissance is the precursor to exploitation. A scanner that maps exposed banking services and open ports builds the target list for the next stage. Separating a persistent, targeted scanner - especially one also flagged as an active exploiter - from internet noise lets the SOC pre-empt exploitation rather than chase blocked probes.

Assets.AssetType: JCB internet-facing services behind NETSCOUT AED (bank range 91.223.202.0/24 - Internet Banking, OWA, middleware and web properties organised into AED protection groups)

LogSources.LogSource: NETSCOUT Arbor Edge Defense CEF - logs-cef.log-*

TelemetryRequirements.Requirement: NETSCOUT AED CEF (verified live on JCB). Populated fields: source.ip, source.geo.country_name, source.as.organization.name, destination.ip, destination.port, cef.extensions.deviceCustomString6 (threat category, e.g. "Network Scanners", "Open Proxies", "Tor Nodes", "Active Exploiters"), cef.device.event_class_id (detection class), cef.extensions.deviceCustomString2 (protection group / bank service), cef.severity, cef.extensions.deviceCustomNumber2 (AED host score, ~0-100).

Population caveat (verified on JCB): for NETSCOUT AED events the web-oriented fields (cef.extensions.requestUrl, requestMethod, deviceHostName, deviceCustomString1/4/5) and event.action are typically null - do not build logic on them. Scan breadth is measured from destination.ip / destination.port fan-out.

Signal.Name: Source Flagged as a Network Scanner
Signal.Details: Events matching "*scan*" - AED threat category "Network Scanners" and related reconnaissance categories against bank services.

Input.name: $srcip
Input.description: External source IP that NETSCOUT AED flagged as scanning (source.ip - the alert entity).

InitialAssessment.Rule: Weigh the full evidence story per the ClassificationGuidance - fan-out breadth, threat category, AED host score and whether AED blocked it - not any single fact. High fan-out plus an "Active Exploiters" flag is far more serious than a single blocked probe from a Tor node.

Investigation.Goal: Determine whether the flagged source is conducting targeted reconnaissance of JCB attack surface (scan breadth, services probed, reputation) and whether it also shows exploitation intent, versus blocked internet background noise.

Step.name: Scan breadth and targets for the source
Step.Purpose: Fan-out is the scan signature: how many distinct destination IPs and ports the source touched, which bank services (protection groups), and where it originates.
Step.Query: FROM logs-cef.log-* | WHERE observer.vendor == "NETSCOUT" AND source.ip == "$srcip" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | STATS events = COUNT(*), dst_ips = COUNT_DISTINCT(destination.ip), dst_ports = COUNT_DISTINCT(destination.port), threat_cats = VALUES(cef.extensions.deviceCustomString6), classes = VALUES(cef.device.event_class_id), services = VALUES(cef.extensions.deviceCustomString2), country = VALUES(source.geo.country_name), asn = VALUES(source.as.organization.name) | LIMIT 1
Step.AnalystNotes: Many distinct dst_ips and/or dst_ports from one source = horizontal/vertical scanning (real recon). A single destination/port touched once is background noise. Note the ASN and country - a hosting/VPS ASN sweeping many bank IPs is typical scanner infrastructure. Grounding: observed live JCB scanners touch ~10-15 bank IPs across ~15 ports each in a 4h window.

Step.name: Reputation, AED host score and category mix
Step.Purpose: The AED threat category, host score and severity separate a benign-reputation scanner from a known-bad host - and reveal exploitation intent if "Active Exploiters" appears.
Step.Query: FROM logs-cef.log-* | WHERE observer.vendor == "NETSCOUT" AND source.ip == "$srcip" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | STATS events = COUNT(*), max_score = MAX(cef.extensions.deviceCustomNumber2), dst_ips = COUNT_DISTINCT(destination.ip), severities = VALUES(cef.severity) BY cef.extensions.deviceCustomString6 | SORT events DESC | LIMIT 15
Step.AnalystNotes: A source appearing only under "Network Scanners"/"Open Proxies"/"Tor Nodes" with a low score is reconnaissance. The same source ALSO appearing under "Active Exploiters" or "Botnet Command and Control" escalates it from recon to attempted exploitation - hand to L2. A high AED host score (deviceCustomNumber2) reflects AED's own confidence the host is malicious.

Step.name: Scan map - which bank IPs and ports were probed
Step.Purpose: The concrete list of destination IPs, services and ports probed shows what attack surface the adversary now knows about and where to check exposure.
Step.Query: FROM logs-cef.log-* | WHERE observer.vendor == "NETSCOUT" AND source.ip == "$srcip" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | STATS hits = COUNT(*), ports = VALUES(destination.port), cats = VALUES(cef.extensions.deviceCustomString6) BY destination.ip, cef.extensions.deviceCustomString2 | SORT hits DESC | LIMIT 20
Step.AnalystNotes: Cross-check the probed destination.ip / protection group against genuinely exposed services. Probing of sensitive ports (e.g. 3389/RDP, 22/SSH, 23/Telnet, DB ports) on a real bank service is higher priority than probing a dark IP. Confirm each probed service was blocked at the perimeter and is patched.

Node.Condition: The source (or its /24 cluster) shows high fan-out across many bank IPs/ports and ALSO appears under "Active Exploiters" / "Botnet Command and Control", or probed a genuinely exposed sensitive service.
Meaningful fan-out flagged "Network Scanners" against bank services, fully blocked by AED, no exploitation category and no exposed-service reach.
Node.Result: True Positive (Reconnaissance - blocked; monitor and blocklist)

Node.Condition: Single/low-volume probing from a Tor node / open proxy / generic internet-noise source, blocked by AED with a low host score.
Node.Result: False Positive (internet background scanning, proven-blocked) or authorised scanner

Node.Condition: High fan-out or an exploitation-category flag, but scope/exposure of the probed services cannot be confirmed from available telemetry.

FalsePositive.Definition: An authorised scanner (e.g. a contracted vulnerability-assessment vendor or asset-discovery service) OR proven-blocked internet background scanning - not an adversary gaining any advantage. Never classify simply as "benign".

Indicators.Item: Source is a known/approved scanner or matches a scheduled external assessment window.
Low fan-out, low AED host score, single "Network Scanners"/"Tor Nodes"/"Open Proxies" category, every event blocked by AED.
No probing of genuinely exposed services and no exploitation category.

SOCAction.Item: Confirm the authorised scanner or the fully-blocked noise; document; close as authorised/proven-blocked. Optionally blocklist noisy sources; tune AED if a known-good scanner keeps alerting.

TruePositive.Definition: Targeted reconnaissance of JCB attack surface: broad or focused scanning of bank services, especially a source that also shows exploitation intent or reaches an exposed service.

Indicators.Item: High destination-IP / port fan-out, or a coordinated source /24 sweeping bank ranges.
Source also flagged "Active Exploiters" / "Botnet Command and Control", or a high AED host score.
Probing of real, exposed banking services / sensitive ports; repeated or persistent activity.

SOCAction.Item: Blocklist the source (and its /24 where clustered) at the perimeter; verify the probed services are patched and not reachable; watch for follow-on exploitation from the same source/ASN; if exploitation categories are present, hand to L2/IR.

Phase.name: Immediate Actions (0-30 minutes)
Phase.Action: Assess fan-out and category mix (INV-01/INV-02). If the source also shows an exploitation category or a high host score, escalate immediately.
Confirm AED blocked the probes and identify which real bank services/ports were targeted (INV-03).
Rule out an authorised/scheduled external scan before treating it as adversarial.

Phase.name: Containment and Eradication (hours)
Phase.Action: Blocklist the source IP and, where a coordinated /24 is evident, the range; verify patch and exposure status of every probed service; correlate the source/ASN against WAF and firewall logs for follow-on attempts.

Phase.name: Recovery and Hardening (days)
Phase.Action: Reduce attack surface on exposed services; feed the scanner IPs/ASN into perimeter blocklists and threat hunting; tune AED categories; review whether any probed service should be internet-facing at all.

Escalation.Trigger: The source also appears under an exploitation category ("Active Exploiters"/"Botnet Command and Control"), reaches a genuinely exposed bank service, or a coordinated multi-IP scanning campaign against bank ranges is evident.

FalsePositiveClosure.Item: Authorised scanner or fully-blocked internet noise confirmed and documented; no exposed-service reach; source optionally blocklisted.

TruePositiveClosure.Item: Source (and /24 where relevant) blocklisted; probed services confirmed patched and not reachable; follow-on activity checked across WAF/firewall; recon campaign documented and added to hunting.
